units.title: Helpdesk Answers gives agents cited answers from help articles
units.claim: Support agents ask about a customer's problem and get a short answer drawn from help articles, with a citation for every claim.
units.explanation: L0: the system and its purpose.

units.title: Two external systems: the CMS and a model provider
units.claim: The system depends on the Help Center CMS (where articles are written) and an external language model provider (which generates the answer text).

units.title: Agent Console is the web client
units.claim: Agents use the Agent Console, a web client that sends each question to the Answers API over HTTPS.

units.title: Answers API checks the session and forwards
units.claim: The Answers API checks the agent's session and forwards the question to the Orchestrator.

units.title: The Orchestrator owns the answering logic
units.claim: The Orchestrator owns answering: it calls Retrieval, sends candidates to the Reranker, calls the Model Gateway and writes every answer with its citations to the Answer log. It has four parts.
units.explanation: L1 component whose internals are L2.

units.title: Only the Model Gateway talks to the model provider
units.claim: The Model Gateway is the only component allowed to talk to the external model provider.
units.explanation: An architectural constraint; it belongs on the Gateway's own card.

units.title: Retrieval finds candidate passages in the Vector store
units.claim: The Retrieval service finds candidate passages by reading from the Vector store. It has two parts.
units.explanation: L1 component whose internals are L2.

units.title: The Reranker reranks candidates
units.claim: The Orchestrator sends candidate passages to the Reranker service.
units.explanation: L1 component. The source says nothing about its internals or code.

units.title: Vector store: Postgres with pgvector
units.claim: The Vector store is a Postgres database with the pgvector extension.

units.title: Answer log keeps every answer with citations
units.claim: Every answer is written, with its citations, to the Answer log table.

units.title: Ingestion refreshes passages every 15 minutes
units.claim: The Ingestion worker reads published articles from the Help Center CMS every 15 minutes, splits them into passages and writes their embeddings to the Vector store.
units.explanation: L1 component; its internals are not described.

units.title: Not specified: ingestion internals, partitioning, two code locations
units.claim: The design does not describe the Ingestion worker's internals, has not decided how the Vector store is partitioned, and gives no code locations for the Ingestion worker or the Reranker.
units.explanation: Known unknowns. They must stay visible as unknown, never be filled with plausible detail.

omission.reason: Without it a reader assumes the gaps are simply not drawn yet.

units.title: Rerank client sends candidates and applies the fallback
units.claim: The Rerank client sends candidates to the Reranker and applies its fallback rule.

units.title: Context builder turns passages into a prompt
units.claim: The Context builder turns the chosen passages into a prompt.

units.title: Answer composer runs the request end to end
units.claim: The Answer composer runs the request from start to finish.
units.explanation: L2 part of the Orchestrator; the flow (L3) is its detail.

units.title: Citation checker: every citation must point to a supplied passage
units.claim: The Citation checker verifies that each citation in a draft answer points to one of the supplied passages.

units.title: Query embedder must use the ingestion's embedding model
units.claim: The Query embedder turns the question into a vector with the same embedding model as the Ingestion worker.
units.explanation: L2 part of Retrieval; the same-model requirement is the point.

units.title: Vector search returns the 50 nearest passages
units.claim: Vector search asks the Vector store for the 50 passages closest to the query vector.

units.title: 1–2: the question arrives and is forwarded
units.claim: The Agent Console posts the question with the ticket id to POST /v1/answers; the Answers API checks the session and forwards it to the Answer composer.

units.title: 3: fetch 50 candidates
units.claim: The Answer composer asks the Retrieval service for 50 candidate passages.

units.title: 4: rerank 50, keep the top 8
units.claim: The Rerank client sends the 50 candidates to the Reranker and keeps the top 8.

units.title: No reply in 800 ms: skip reranking, flag it
units.claim: If the Reranker does not respond within 800 ms, reranking is skipped, the first 8 candidates are kept in vector-similarity order and rerank_skipped = true is logged; faster, but the 8 passages may be less relevant.
units.explanation: The failure path of step 4. It limits step 4 and must sit with it.

units.title: 5: composeAnswer with the 8 passages
units.claim: The Answer composer calls composeAnswer with the question and the 8 passages.
units.explanation: L3 flow, step 5; its detail is the L4 operation.

units.title: 6–7: log the answer, return it
units.claim: The answer and its citations are written to the Answer log, and the Answers API returns the answer to the Agent Console.

units.title: composeAnswer: prompt ≤ 6,000 tokens, model call, citation check
units.claim: composeAnswer(question, passages) builds the prompt with the Context builder, limited to 6000 tokens, calls the Model Gateway and passes the draft to the Citation checker.

units.title: Model timeout after 20 s: HTTP 504, no partial answer
units.claim: The model call times out after 20 seconds; composeAnswer then returns an error, the API responds with HTTP 504 and no partial answer is shown.

units.title: Unmatched citation: drop the sentence, mark partial
units.claim: If a citation matches no supplied passage, composeAnswer removes the sentence that carries it and marks the answer as partial instead of rejecting the whole answer.
units.explanation: L4 failure path. Note the contrast with the timeout path (partial here, never partial there).
mustPreserve: rather than rejecting the whole answer

units.title: composeAnswer lives in compose.ts, lines 40–118
units.claim: composeAnswer is in services/orchestrator/src/compose.ts, lines 40–118.
units.explanation: L5 evidence for the L4 operation.

paraphrase.note: Paths and line ranges are exact.

units.title: checkCitations lives in citations.ts
units.claim: The citation check is checkCitations in services/orchestrator/src/citations.ts.

units.title: Vector search lives in search.ts
units.claim: Vector search is search in services/retrieval/src/search.ts.
units.explanation: Code evidence for the L2 Vector search component.

mustNotClaim.claim: Any code path for the Ingestion worker or the Reranker (e.g. services/ingestion/…, services/reranker/…).
mustNotClaim.why: The source says no code locations are given for them.

mustNotClaim.claim: A partitioning or sharding scheme for the Vector store.
Code for composeAnswer (a function body or signature beyond composeAnswer(question, passages)).
mustNotClaim.why: The source gives a location, not code.

mustNotClaim.claim: Components other than the Model Gateway call the model provider.
mustNotClaim.why: The Gateway is the only allowed path.

mustNotClaim.claim: A timed-out request returns a partial answer, or an unmatched citation rejects the whole answer.
mustNotClaim.why: The two failure paths are opposite; swapping them is a distortion.

mustNotClaim.claim: Skipping reranking makes the answer wrong.
mustNotClaim.why: The source only says the passages may be less relevant.
